clue.text: Garment cherished, exactly fitting I see

parts.note: a pet is a cherished, favoured one

indicators.note: the pair of letters is fitted into the phrase for 'exactly'

parts.note: 'to a T' means exactly, precisely
I plus C, the letter whose name sounds like 'see'

explanation.surface: Someone admires a cherished item of clothing that fits perfectly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I see' is a stock crossword device: I plus C, the letter named like 'see'. 'Exactly' is the idiom 'to a T'.
explanation.definitionFit: A petticoat is an underskirt, a woman's undergarment worn beneath a dress.

clue.text: Father standing, he offers a salutation, its elements warming

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
up means standing, out of bed
one who raises a glass in salute is a toaster

explanation.surface: A dad gets to his feet to make a toast, his speech warming the room.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the appliance whose heating elements warm the bread.
explanation.definitionFit: The kitchen appliance browns bread using glowing electric elements that warm it.

clue.text: See 1
Nursing cold, one doubled up lay disheartened, with very little warmth

indicators.note: the doubled numeral holds the cold letter between its two copies
the numeral is written twice in a row

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: the word lay loses its central letter, its heart

explanation.surface: A sick person, nursing a cold and doubled over, lay in a chilly room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes the middle A from LAY, leaving LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking coldly, with a frosty manner, is an adverb of distant unfriendliness.

clue.text: Manage some poetry in the middle of poem

indicators.note: the poetry word goes inside the central letters
only the central letters of poem are kept, O and E

parts.note: verse is a portion of poetry

explanation.surface: An editor handles a bit of verse placed in the centre of a longer poem.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise or direct work is to manage it.

clue.text: Land — there's failure to include it within the borders of Turkey

indicators.note: the combined piece sits between the edge letters of Turkey
only the first and last letters of Turkey, T and Y
the word for failure takes in the small word it

parts.note: an error is a failure or mistake

explanation.surface: A border dispute: a failure to include some land within Turkey's frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there's' is just a link; the dash separates the definition from the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Territory is an area of land under a ruler's control.

clue.text: Help us to get round OK

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal asking for help
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone asks for help getting around, insisting they are fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Middling, merely passable, so only all right or tolerable.

clue.text: See 24
Necking drinks, pursue patter

indicators.note: swallowing, so the word for pursue holds the drinks inside it

parts.note: to stalk is to pursue or follow
ales are drinks of beer

explanation.surface: A drinker downing beers while chasing someone and chatting them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Necking' is British slang for drinking quickly, and here signals one piece swallowed by another.
explanation.definitionFit: Patter is a smooth persuasive line, like a seller's pitch to customers.

clue.text: Expressing desire, top kinky musical making a comeback

indicators.note: twisted, so the letters of top are rearranged
the show's name is written backwards

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical

explanation.surface: A wish for a top-notch, raunchy musical to return to the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kinky' turns TOP into OPT; 'making a comeback' turns EVITA into ATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The optative is the grammatical mood used for wishes and expressions of hope.

clue.text: Burrow oft hollow in part

indicators.note: the hollowed word sits inside the word for part

parts.note: a role is an actor's part

indicators.note: emptied of its middle, so only the outside letters of oft remain

explanation.surface: An animal often burrows into a hollow in part of the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To rootle is to dig or rummage about, as a pig does with its snout.

clue.text: Start to yawn on a course, showing lack of interest

indicators.note: in an across clue, the yawn letter is placed after the earlier pieces

parts.note: a path is a course or route

indicators.note: just the opening letter of yawn

explanation.surface: A bored student begins yawning on a course, plainly uninterested.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is indifference, the absence of enthusiasm or concern.

clue.text: Medical assessment most impoverished?

definitions.meaning: a check of how the body's outer layer reacts to an allergen
skint is slang for broke, so jokingly its superlative with -est

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a medical check reveals who is the poorest.
explanation.definitionFit: A patch or prick test on the body's surface checks for allergies; read as one word it is a jokey superlative of broke.

clue.text: Tear back and forth as Dickensian protagonist

indicators.note: the word for tear is read backwards first

parts.note: rip means tear
then the same word read forwards

explanation.surface: Someone rips something back and forth like a character in Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: RIP backwards then forwards gives a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Pirrip, known as Pip, is the narrator and hero of Great Expectations.

clue.text: Silly saving last bit in doggy bag, upended regardless

indicators.note: the word for silly keeps the pieces safe inside it

parts.note: inane means silly

indicators.note: only the final letter of doggy
turned over, so the word for bag reads upwards in this down clue

parts.note: a sac is a bag or pouch

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly saves the last scraps in a doggy bag, tipped upside down anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upended' only works as a reversal because this is a down entry, read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyhow, whatever happens: the phrase means regardless of circumstances.

clue.text: Patriarch John squeezing alongside Protestant elder

indicators.note: the legendary name holds the small word tight inside

parts.note: Prester John was the legendary Christian priest-king
by means beside, alongside

explanation.surface: A church patriarch named John squeezes in beside a Protestant elder.
explanation.definitionFit: In Presbyterian churches the presbyter is an elder governing the congregation.

clue.text: Nutty green apple finally getting shredded for cake

indicators.note: just the last letter of apple
torn up, so the letters of for cake are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe: shred an apple for a nutty cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nutty' looks like part of the recipe but is in the definition: a green who is nuts about the environment.
explanation.definitionFit: A green is an environmentalist; a nutty one is a zealot for the cause.

clue.text: Work on beach that is in US city

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the combined pieces
the word for work comes after the word for beach

parts.note: sand is what a beach is made of
go means work, function
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Someone works on a beach in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: A major city on the coast of California, near the Mexican border.

clue.text: Filth around capital in Louisiana, live American strip

indicators.note: the word for filth goes round the other pieces

parts.note: dirt is filth

indicators.note: the capital, that is first, letter of Louisiana

parts.note: to be is to live, exist

explanation.surface: Dirt in Louisiana's capital, as described in some lurid American report.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scott Adams office comic strip, an American newspaper cartoon.

clue.text: Red chevron with flash clothing turning up like this, style for a bowler

indicators.note: everything is read upwards in this down clue
the word for a moment wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: a mo, a moment, is a flash
rare meat is red
a chevron is a V shape

explanation.surface: A uniformed figure with red stripes and a badge gestures upwards to demonstrate.
explanation.walkthrough: MO holds RAREV to give MRAREVO, which 'turning up' reverses. 'like this' points to the bowling arm action.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a bowler delivers the ball with the arm raised above the shoulder.

clue.text: Duck I caught in the air recalled hunter's cry

indicators.note: the three pieces go inside the backwards word
called back, so the word for the air is written backwards

parts.note: the sky is the air above
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cricketer out for nothing remembers the hunting cry in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional fox-hunting shout urging the hounds on.

clue.text: In a plain way, said like this clue?

definitions.meaning: simply, without long or complicated language
every word of the clue is short, a single beat long

explanation.surface: A clue that announces how it is written.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means very simply, avoiding difficult terms; each word here has just one beat.

clue.text: See 20
Sensation of the East End, Barking, is it?

parts.note: Bow is a district in London's East End
a wow is a sensational hit

explanation.surface: A sensational place in the East End, Barking, is it?
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is also an East London district, misleading as a place name; Bow is in London's East End.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's word for a dog, imitating its barking sound.

clue.text: Wearing something black for Halloween? Give us a twirl!

parts.note: a bat is a black Halloween creature or costume
on means being worn

explanation.surface: A trick-or-treater in a black bat costume is asked to spin round and show it off.
explanation.definitionFit: A majorette or drum major twirls this stick, so it invites a twirl.

clue.text: See 20
King Edward holds advanced position for scout

indicators.note: the potato word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a King Edward is a variety of potato; tater is slang for potato
lent money is advanced money
a spot is a position

explanation.surface: A king holds an advanced post, as a military scout might.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a common British potato variety.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who seeks out promising performers or players, as a scout does.

clue.text: Soldier with fury moving to the back or to the front

indicators.note: joins the soldier to the following pieces

parts.note: a soldier ant is a kind of ant

indicators.note: the word for fury goes backwards

parts.note: ire is fury

explanation.surface: A soldier in a rage advances or retreats.
explanation.definitionFit: Situated at the front, as opposed to posterior.

clue.text: Home in one's tree

indicators.note: the letters are found within the words one's tree

explanation.surface: A home in someone's tree, like a treehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's dwelling where it raises its young.

clue.text: Look back on nicer times, less hurt ultimately different

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged into something different
only the last letter of hurt

explanation.surface: Remembering nicer times, now less painful in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes T from NICER TIMES; 'different' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall past experiences fondly is to look back on them.
